post.text: Alright, long one today because a lot of you asked for my full view after the Fed meeting. First, macro: rates are not coming down as fast as the market priced in March, and that is fine. Liquidity is still improving at the margin, stablecoin supply on-chain is up for the fourth month in a row, and funding rates across the majors have reset to roughly neutral after the flush last week. That is the kind of setup I like, because the leverage is gone and spot is doing the work. Second, the L2 sector. Fees are tiny now, activity keeps moving off mainnet, and the token unlock overhang that everyone was scared of in the summer is mostly behind us. Sequencer revenue is real, small but real. So yes, I am buying $OP here and I think you should too, sized sensibly, with the low from last Tuesday as my line in the sand. Third, what I am not doing: I am not chasing the new launches, I am not touching anything with an unlock in the next sixty days, and I am keeping a cash buffer for the usual end-of-quarter volatility. Questions in the comments, I will try to answer all of them.

post.text: Thread on where I stand going into the new year, since people keep asking in DMs. I have been in this market since 2017 and the one thing I have learned is that the cycle punishes people who keep changing their plan. My plan has not changed. I hold $BTC and $ETH in cold storage, I have held them through two bear markets, and I am not selling them this cycle either. I am also not adding at these prices. I think $BTC can reach 200k sometime in 2027 and $ETH can outperform once the staking narrative comes back, but those are views, not trades. The rest of my portfolio is boring: index funds, a bit of cash, and a house I am still paying off. If you are new, the best advice I can give is to stop reading threads like this one at 3am, write your own plan down, and stick to it when the chart looks scary. Nobody on this app knows the future, including me. Happy holidays and see you on the other side of the halving talk.
